intended_object: The canonical group isomorphism U_n(R) ≅ Hom_{Spec K}(Spec R, U_n). It identifies the group of upper unitriangular n×n matrices over a commutative K-algebra R with the R-points of the affine group scheme U_n over Spec K, as in Milne §2.8–2.9. I took this from the docstring, the module documentation and the name.
explanation:
The definition composes two group isomorphisms:

1. `unitriangularGroupMulEquivAlgHom` sends a unitriangular matrix to the K-algebra map from the Hopf quotient coordinate ring to R that evaluates the coordinates on it. Its group structure is the convolution product.
2. `Spec.mapMulEquiv` identifies K-algebra maps from that coordinate ring to R with morphisms over Spec K from Spec R to its Spec, as a group isomorphism.

The source, `Matrix.UnitriangularGroup n R`, is the subgroup of GL_n(R) of matrices that are upper triangular with ones on the diagonal. That is the standard unitriangular group. The target is the set of R-points of `unitriangularGroupUnderlyingScheme K n`, which is Spec of the coordinate ring viewed as a scheme over Spec K.

The generality is natural:
- K is any commutative ring.
- R is any commutative K-algebra.
- n is any finite linearly ordered index type. The order is needed to say "upper triangular".
- All types live in one universe u. This is the usual constraint for Spec and points in Mathlib.

Mathlib has no unitriangular group scheme or comparison of its points, so there is no counterpart to cite. Overall, the definition is the standard functor-of-points identification at its natural generality.
